key_insight: The best way to predict low-energy subspace overlap depends on the dynamical regime: shadow-based learning wins for moderate quenches, while physics-informed QCNNs are more robust across weak, moderate, and strong quenches.
engineering_relevance: This work guides when to use measurement-efficient classical pipelines versus coherent quantum processing for quantum state diagnostics in many-body simulators and future quantum devices.
method: Classical shadows + CNNs for measurement-based prediction of overlap O_K
QCNNs that act directly on the quantum state for coherent learning
Physics-informed variants using Hamiltonian-aware shadows and Heisenberg-aligned QCNN gates
evidence_signal: Across five quench datasets, physics-informed QCNNs achieved mean test R^2 of 0.753–0.846, while shadow methods peaked at R^2 = 0.886 in the moderate-quench regime but dropped to 0.615 and 0.672 in weak and strong quenches at default shot budgets.
watch_item: Hardware realism is a major challenge: state preparation dominates the cost, with roughly 2,044 two-qubit gates leading to near-complete depolarization before inference.
paper_title: Learning Low-Energy Subspace Overlaps in Many-Body Systems with Measurement-Based and Coherent Quantum Strategies
